messages:
customer_acct: Hey team — our production service started getting 429s yesterday evening. Quota in the console for the project looks fine (250k/min), but traffic is low. Request IDs: `req_0a1b2c3d` and `req_0a1b2c3e`. Any idea why we're being limited?

alex_support: Sorry about that — can you paste a sample curl and the response headers you saw? Also which API key + project id were used? :eyes:

customer_acct: Sample (proxying through our infra):
```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXXX" \n  -H "X-Forwarded-For: 34.102.123.45" \n  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Response headers we got: `X-Redwood-RateLimit: 429`, `Retry-After: 12`. Console shows project `proj-42` using ~12k/min. The NAT IP 34.102.123.45 is shared across 3 of our projects.

alex_support: Thanks. Two quick things: 1) are you definitely sending the same `Authorization` on every request (no token rotation mishap)? 2) do you have any intermediate proxies that might strip the header so requests sometimes land without a key?

customer_acct: We rotate keys but it's centralised. I double-checked logs — the header is present for these failing requests. Also saw entries where key is present but `x-forwarded-for` is different.

lee_sre: Quick summary of the behavior we've seen in similar incidents: our rate limiter attempts attribution in this order (short form): API key -> project binding -> org-wide quotas -> IP fallback. If a request arrives with a valid API key, the limiter charges the key/project bucket. If the key is invalid/missing or the routing layer rewrites it, we fall back to IP-based buckets (shared NATs can hit limits quickly). Edge-case: if the key is valid but comes from a NAT'd address that has already exhausted an IP bucket (we apply a per-IP safety cap), you may still see temporary 429s while IP-level protections sync.

maria_plat: Adding: there is also a burst/token-bucket behavior — if many concurrent short requests from the same NAT arrive, the per-IP burst reservoir can be drained even if the project bucket is healthy. That is intentional to protect multitenant NAT carriers.

customer_acct: Ah — so even with a valid key we can be limited by the IP safety cap? That would explain the mismatch vs console. Any way to confirm it from our side?

lee_sre: Yes. To confirm, ask us for the raw request log lines (we can filter by `req_0a1b2c3d`). If the limiter applied an IP fallback rule you'll see a log like: `limiter.attribution=ip fallback, bucket=ip:34.102.123.45, reason=ip-over-threshold`. If you can't share full logs here, paste the header block from the failing response (some headers include `X-Rate-Limit-Source: ip` or `X-Redwood-Attribution: ip` depending on version).

alex_support: Workarounds while we investigate: 1) Have your infra preserve and forward a unique X-Client-Project header and request a project binding from support — we can apply stronger project-level affinity for that header temporarily. 2) If you can move some steady traffic to a different egress IP range or dedicate an outbound NAT to this project, that'll avoid the shared-IP cap. 3) As a short-term mitigation we can bump your project burst allowance (requires auth escalation).

customer_acct: We'll try to flip a dedicated NAT for a subset of traffic to prove it. Can you also confirm whether 429s from IP-capping are billed? We're tracking unexpected billing breaks.

maria_plat: 429s due to rate limiting are not charged for the refused request bodies (we don't bill tokens that weren't accepted/processed). However partial request work (e.g., connections accepted and some tokens generated before a limiter kicked in) can have small billed usage — send examples and we'll audit.

alex_support: I'll open a scoped escalation with infra to look for `req_0a1b2c3d|e` and the NAT ip range. If you post the dedicated NAT IP when ready we can whitelist it to bypass IP safety caps for a short window. :thumbsup:

rate-limiter-bot: autoticket #SR-10234 created -> SRE assigned: lee_sre. ETA 4h for initial findings.

customer_acct: Thanks — sending dedicated NAT details in DM and will share a failing response header verbatim. Appreciate the quick help.
